sentences.ar: خلينا نبني الـfunnel ده بالأرقام عشان نشوفه بيشتغل إزاي عملي
sentences.en: Let's build this funnel with numbers to see how it works in practice.

sentences.ar: بعد كده بتدخل مرحلة WHERE الفلتر ده طير الـcancelled order 1004 وrefunded order 1010
sentences.en: Then the WHERE stage kicks in: this filter dropped cancelled order 1004 and refunded order 1010.

sentences.ar: وكده الـfunnel نزل بينه من 13 صف لـ11 صف بس
sentences.en: So the funnel took us from 13 rows down to just 11.

sentences.ar: ولما بنوصل للـGROUP BY الـ11 صف دول بينضغطوا بقوة ويبقوا 2 groups بس شريحة الـgold وشريحة الـsilver
sentences.en: When we reach GROUP BY, those 11 rows are compressed hard into just 2 groups: the gold tier and the silver tier.

sentences.ar: شايفين الـfunnel شغال ازاي؟ بدأ بـ14 بعدين 13 نزل لـ 11 لحد ما وصل لـ 2
sentences.en: See how the funnel works? It started at 14, then 13, dropped to 11, until it reached 2.

sentences.ar: النتيجة دي بتأكد أن شغلنا وتجمعنا مظبوط جداً
sentences.en: This result confirms our work and our aggregation are exactly right.

sentences.ar: لو جمعنا مبيعات الـgold اللي هي 3098 .30 سنت يورو مع مبيعات الـsilver اللي هي 850 .20 سنت يورو هنلاقي الإجمالي 3948 .5 يورو
sentences.en: If we add gold sales of 3098.30 euros to silver sales of 850.20 euros, we get a total of 3948.5 euros.

sentences.ar: الرقم ده بيثبت أن pipeline الديتا بتاعنا سليم 100 % من البداية للنهاية من غير ما أي ديتا تضيع في السكة
sentences.en: This number proves our data pipeline is 100% sound from start to finish, with no data lost along the way.

sentences.ar: ومن هنا بيجي أشهر error في الـSQL كله
sentences.en: And this brings us to the most famous error in all of SQL.

sentences.ar: ليه لو كتبنا WHERE revenue أكبر من 300 الكود بيفشل
sentences.en: Why does the code fail if we write WHERE revenue greater than 300?

sentences.ar: السر في الـfunnel الـalias اللي اسمه revenue بيتولد في المرحلة السادسة عند SELECT
sentences.en: The secret is in the funnel: the alias named revenue is born at the sixth stage, at SELECT.

sentences.ar: لكن الـWHERE بتشتغل بدري جداً في المرحلة الثالثة يعني الـWHERE عمرها ما سمعت عن حاجة اسمها revenue أصلاً
sentences.en: But WHERE runs very early, at the third stage, so WHERE has never even heard of anything called revenue.

sentences.ar: الحل الصح هنا هو استخدام HAVING SUM أو إننا نستخدم CTE
sentences.en: The right fix here is to use HAVING SUM, or to use a CTE.

sentences.ar: رقم 5 الـgrain والـLIMIT 1
sentences.en: Number 5: the grain and LIMIT 1.

sentences.ar: وهنا نيجي لتاني سؤال توقع معنا وده سؤال بيلخبط ناس تقيلة وخبرة في المجال
sentences.en: Here we come to our second prediction question, one that confuses heavyweights with experience in the field.

sentences.ar: لو حطينا LIMIT 1 في آخر الـquery هل ده معناه أن المحرك فعلاً بيوفر مجهود وحسابات تحت الكابوت؟ تفتكروا أيوة ولا لأ؟
sentences.en: If we put LIMIT 1 at the end of the query, does the engine really save effort and computation under the hood? Yes or no?

sentences.ar: المفاجأة؟ لا طبعاً المحرك لسه مضطر يحسب ويرتب كل الـgroups بالكامل عشان يقدر يعرف مين الفايز الأول اللي هيرجع
sentences.en: The surprise? Of course not: the engine still has to compute and sort all the groups fully to know which winner comes first.

sentences.ar: كل اللي الـLIMIT بتعمله إنها بتقلل حجم الديتا اللي بتتبيعت على الشبكة لكنها مش بتوفر أي مجهود حسابي
sentences.en: All LIMIT does is reduce the amount of data sent over the network; it doesn't save any computation.

sentences.ar: يعني الـfunnel بتاعنا بيوصل لـ1 في الآخر بس بعد ما الشغل تقيل كله تعمل
sentences.en: So our funnel ends at 1, but only after all the heavy work has been done.

sentences.ar: الجداول العلاقتية الصارمة مش دايماً هي الحل السحري لكل حاجة
sentences.en: Strict relational tables aren't always the magic solution for everything.

sentences.ar: في عوالم الـ NoSQL المذهلة عندنا حلول تانية بتناسب احتياجات مختلفة
sentences.en: In the amazing worlds of NoSQL we have other solutions that suit different needs.

sentences.ar: الـ Document زي MongoDB الممتاز في الـschema زي متدخلة
sentences.en: Document stores like MongoDB, great at nested schemas.

sentences.ar: الـ Key-value زي Redis بطل الـcaching بسرعته الرهيبة مع TTL 3600
sentences.en: Key-value like Redis, the caching champion with its blazing speed, with a TTL of 3600.

sentences.ar: الـ Wide-column زي Cassandra اللي بيتصمم حسب الـquery مع Replication Factor 3
sentences.en: Wide-column like Cassandra, designed around the query, with a replication factor of 3.

sentences.ar: وأخيراً الـGraph زي Neo4j العبقري في تتبع العلاقات وأقصر مسار
sentences.en: And finally graph databases like Neo4j, brilliant at tracing relationships and shortest paths.

sentences.ar: وبكده بنوصل للمخرجات النهائية لتصميمنا مخطط الـ ERD، ملف DDL، و6 queries كل واحدة مكتوب عليها الـgrain بتاعها بوضوح
sentences.en: That brings us to our design's final outputs: the ERD diagram, a DDL file, and 6 queries, each clearly labeled with its grain.

sentences.ar: سؤال الختامي ليكم بعد كل ده هل أنتوا جاهزين تبنوا معمارية الداتا بتاعتكم بوعي وأصدى حقيقي؟
sentences.en: Our closing question after all this: are you ready to build your data architecture with real awareness?

sentences.ar: وهل هتبقوا عارفين الـgrain بتاع كل الصف قبل ما تكتبوا الـquery اللي جاية؟
sentences.en: And will you know the grain of every row before you write your next query?

sentences.ar: نتمنى تكون الرحلة دي نورت نقاط كتير مهمة شكراً لكم
sentences.en: We hope this journey shed light on many important points. Thank you.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: A stage-by-stage view in which rows shrink at each step, such as join, filter and group,…
concepts.failure: Not counting rows at each stage, so a join silently dropping rows goes unnoticed.

concepts.def_en: One record in a table: a single entity or event, with one value for each column.
concepts.failure: A bad join duplicates rows, silently inflating every total.

concepts.def_en: SQL clause that splits rows into groups sharing the same key values, so aggregates like S…
concepts.failure: Grouping on a dirty key, so one customer splits into many groups.

concepts.def_en: A chain of automated steps where each stage's output feeds the next, such as extract, tra…
concepts.failure: Not making steps idempotent, so a rerun duplicates or corrupts data.

concepts.def_en: A message or failure signalling that something went wrong; read it first, since it usuall…
concepts.failure: Pasting the error into a search engine without first reading the terminal output.

concepts.def_en: Structured Query Language: the standard declarative language for querying and changing da…
concepts.failure: Thinking SQL runs in written order; the engine plans execution in its own order.

concepts.def_en: The SQL clause that chooses which columns or expressions to return, and where aliases are…
concepts.failure: Writing SELECT * in production, pulling columns and resources nobody needs.

concepts.def_en: The clause that filters groups after GROUP BY, using aggregate results such as SUM or COU…
concepts.failure: Filtering an aggregate like SUM in WHERE, which runs before grouping.

concepts.def_en: What exactly one row represents, such as one order line; every metric must be computed at…
concepts.failure: Computing a SUM at the wrong grain, getting a confident but wrong number.

concepts.def_en: SQL clause that caps how many rows a query returns; it runs last, so pair it with ORDER B…
concepts.failure: Using LIMIT without ORDER BY, so which rows come back is arbitrary.

concepts.def_en: A request to a database or search system to fetch, filter or change data; in SQL, usually…
concepts.failure: Blaming hardware for a slow query when a full table scan is the cause.

concepts.def_en: Data organized into rows and columns under a fixed structure; the basic building block of…
concepts.failure: Treating a table like a spreadsheet: mixed meanings, merged cells and no keys.

concepts.def_en: Non-relational databases, such as document, key-value or graph stores, that trade fixed s…
concepts.failure: Assuming NoSQL means no schema, so inconsistent data piles up unnoticed.

concepts.def_en: The declared structure of data: field or column names, types and constraints, which a table or message must follow.
concepts.def_ar: الهيكل المعلن للداتا: أسماء الـfields أو الـcolumns وأنواعها والـconstraints اللي لازم الجدول أو الرسالة تلتزم بيها.
concepts.failure: Changing a field's type or removing it without checking that downstream consumers still work.

concepts.def_en: Keeping copies of frequently used data in faster storage to avoid slower repeated reads, as database caches and Spark's cache do.
concepts.def_ar: الاحتفاظ بنسخة من الداتا المستخدمة كتير في مكان أسرع، عشان نتجنب القراءة البطيئة المتكررة، زي cache الـdatabase والـSpark.
concepts.failure: Serving stale cached data without invalidation, or mistaking cache-filled memory for a leak.

concepts.def_en: Keeping several copies of the same data on different machines, so a failure loses nothing…
concepts.failure: Mistaking replication for backup; a bad delete or corruption copies to every replica.

concepts.def_en: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to model relationships such as roads, dependencie…
concepts.failure: Confusing a graph (nodes and edges) with a chart (plotted data).

concepts.def_en: Entity-relationship diagram: a picture of tables, their keys and the relationships and cardinality between them.
concepts.def_ar: الـERD رسمة بتوضّح الجداول ومفاتيحها والعلاقات بينها والـcardinality بتاعتها.
concepts.failure: Drawing tables without keys or relationship cardinality, leaving the design ambiguous.
